name: Never force push or overwrite repos
description: Never suggest git push --force or overwriting existing repos/branches without explicit confirmation
type: feedback
---

Never suggest `git push --force` to overwrite an existing repo, even if it looks like an old PoC.

**Why:** The existing content might have value, context, or history that isn't obvious. Force-pushing destroys that permanently.

**How to apply:** When pushing to a remote that already has content, always suggest creating a new repo/branch or fetching first. Never default to `--force`.
---
name: feedback-merge-just-commit
description: "Don't run full lint/prettier/tsc passes to \"verify\" a merge — resolve conflicts, commit, push. Both sides already passed their own checks."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: c225d886-900b-4a51-bb80-c772a2963347
---

When merging `main` (or another branch) and conflicts come up, resolve the conflicts and commit. Don't run a full `eslint`/`prettier`/`tsc` sweep across the package "to verify the merge" — both sides already passed their own checks, and pre-existing errors on either side aren't the merge's problem.

**Why:** Sid called this out directly during the main → migration-block-init-staging-branch merge. The rule "run all three checks after changes" was over-applied to merge commits, which exposed pre-existing TS errors in `packages/database/src/lib/contextFunctions.ts` that had nothing to do with the conflict resolution.

**How to apply:**
- For merge commits, focus on conflict resolution correctness, not full re-verification.
- If a conflict resolution looks structurally risky (picked the wrong side, signature mismatch, etc.), do a targeted `tsc --noEmit` on the affected files — not the whole repo.
- Never `git stash` mid-merge to "compare with the pre-merge state." That loses merge state and is destructive. If you need a before/after, use `git show MERGE_HEAD:path` or `git show HEAD~:path` instead.
- Related: [[feedback-pr-scope-discipline]] — merge commits stay scoped to the merge, no opportunistic fixes.
---
name: Minimal merge commit messages
description: For merge commits, use the default git message (one line) — don't write a prose summary of conflict resolutions
type: feedback
originSessionId: da05784b-debd-4e50-9818-223758823d5d
---
For merge commits, use a one-line message — `"Merge origin/main into <branch>"` or whatever the default would be. Do NOT write a multi-paragraph summary of which conflicts were resolved or how.

**Why:** The diff already shows what was resolved. A long prose message in the merge commit body adds noise that the reviewer has to wade through. Past merges on this branch use the default one-liner.

**How to apply:** When committing a merge, use `git commit -m "Merge origin/main into <branch-name>"` — short, matches existing merge commits on the branch. Skip the "here's what I resolved" commentary. Conflict-resolution reasoning belongs in chat, not in the commit message.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# PreToolUse(Bash) hook in the team Claude config (~/.claude-company/settings.json).

set -uo pipefail

input="$(cat)"

cwd="$(jq -r '.cwd // empty' <<<"$input")"

push_re='(^|[;&|(])[[:space:]]*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=[^[:space:]]*[[:space:]]+)*git([[:space:]]+-[Cc][[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]+)*[[:space:]]+push([[:space:]]|$)'
grep -qE "$push_re" <<<"$cmd" || exit 0
grep -qE '(^|[[:space:]])SKIP_PRE_PR_REVIEW=1([[:space:]]|$)' <<<"$cmd" && exit 0

seg="$(grep -oE 'git([[:space:]]+-[Cc][[:space:]]+[^[:space:];&|)]+)*[[:space:]]+push([[:space:]][^;&|)]*)?' <<<"$cmd" | head -1)"
before_push="${cmd%%"$seg"*}"

dir="$cwd"
cd_target="$(grep -oE '(^|[;&(])[[:space:]]*cd[[:space:]]+[^;&|)]+' <<<"$before_push" | tail -1 |
  sed -E 's/^[;&( ]*cd[[:space:]]+//; s/[[:space:]]+$//' | tr -d "\"'")"
if [ -n "$cd_target" ]; then
  cd_target="${cd_target/#\~/$HOME}"
  case "$cd_target" in /*) dir="$cd_target" ;; *) dir="$cwd/$cd_target" ;; esac
fi

read -ra words <<<"$seg"
i=1
while [ "$i" -lt "${#words[@]}" ]; do
  case "${words[$i]}" in
    -C)
      c_path="$(tr -d "\"'" <<<"${words[$((i + 1))]:-}")"
      c_path="${c_path/#\~/$HOME}"
      case "$c_path" in /*) dir="$c_path" ;; *) dir="$dir/$c_path" ;; esac
      i=$((i + 2))
      ;;
    -c) i=$((i + 2)) ;;
    push)
      i=$((i + 1))
      break

    *) i=$((i + 1)) ;;

done

positional=()
for w in "${words[@]:$i}"; do
  case "$w" in

    -*) ;;

rev="HEAD"
if [ "${#positional[@]}" -ge 2 ]; then

A comment referencing context not present in the file (another PR, a discussion, another platform's behavior) either becomes self-contained or dies: reviewers reply "What is F12?" / "What is the same reason?" to comments they can't parse cold (#1315, #1292, #1284). Keep only comments stating a constraint the code can't show.
70:2b. **Provenance trace.** For every value read from a PostgREST response or datalog result used in the diff: name the source column, grep its type in `packages/database/supabase/schemas/*.sql`, then judge the code handling it (timestamps are the known killer — naive UTC, no `Z`).
78:2f. **Flag-gated writes.** For every new DB write path: which user-visible flag or action authorizes it? Sync flag off ⇒ the user expects NO DB communication; a silent maintenance write (backfill, migration) needs explicit call-out in the PR, and its outcome reports to PostHog — never a user toast (#1332).
86:- new UI elements → which flag gates them (including EXISTING flags the new surface must respect, e.g. `autoCanvasRelations` on #1272); user-facing failures → PostHog + toast, not `console.error`
92:- user-facing strings use user vocabulary — a toast saying "backfilled" is a finding; internal bookkeeping reports to PostHog only (#1332)
96:- Every hunk maps to this PR's ticket; unrelated changes → revert or explicitly annotate. Out-of-scope improvements a reviewer might request → pre-empt by naming them in the PR with a Linear ticket ("X is deferred to ENG-YYYY").
98:- **Bot-comment gate.** Before requesting human review: every codex/graphite/devin comment is either fixed or answered with why-not, and resolved. mdroidian's first pass is frequently just "See codex comments" / "address the bot reviews … and click resolve" (#1257, #1309, #1320) — an unresolved bot thread costs a full review round-trip.
99:- **Chain coverage.** For a PR in a stacked or sibling-ticket chain: does the union of this PR + named sibling tickets cover both platforms and both data directions? "This only handles Obsidian-origin — where's Roam-origin?" is maparent's most repeated 07–08 comment (#1267, #1269, #1316). Name the gap and the ticket that owns it in the PR before he does.
100:- **Guard removals are argued in the PR.** Removing an existence check or gate: state the cases it protected and why each is now safe (idempotent re-upsert, upstream guarantee). #1280's check removal survived review, but through a 3-comment thread that one PR annotation would have preempted.
104:- **Inherited decisions carry breadcrumbs.** Any code that exists because of a review decision on a PREVIOUS PR (a reviewer's direction, a contract agreed in another thread) gets a draft line-comment citing that source ("per maparent on #1214: local IDs may already be RIDs"). Without the breadcrumb the next reviewer re-litigates it.
110:2b. **Draft PR annotations** — ready-to-post, line-anchored comments explaining every non-obvious decision (guidepost style: what this block does and why, inherited-decision citations, parity-table deltas). Proven repeatedly: #1214, and in 07–08 reviewers replied to annotations in-thread and accepted the argument (#1280 "I accept this argument. Approving.", #1331). Also annotate every LARGE removal or moved block ("this was refactored into abc.ts") — mdroidian asked for exactly this on #1320. Posting them is part of finishing the PR, not optional polish.
111:2c. All reviewer-facing prose this skill emits — PR description bullets, draft annotations, deferral notes, parity tables — follows the team writing style skill at `<repo-root>/.claude/skills/discourse-engineering-writing-style/SKILL.md` (mdroidian's #1278): lead with the point, one term per concept, replace vague verbs ("handle", "support") with the specific behavior, no em dashes, shortest version that keeps the nuance.
112:3. **Predicted review** (simulation, not identity): given the reviewers' comment history — mdroidian: frontend craftsmanship, dead code, reuse, naming, comment noise, bare `!`, second lookups, design parity with existing UI, reserved vocabulary (Page/Block/Any), unresolved bot comments, demo-video quality, Socratic "why is this here?"; maparent: schema/contract correctness, query shape, the missing converter direction, chain/sibling-ticket coverage gaps ("this only handles Obsidian-origin"), values re-fetched that the pipeline already carries, partial-failure semantics, Obsidian-parity of UX decisions, "worth calling out in another task?", "what does the data look like in 6 months?" — list the comments each would most likely leave on the remaining diff. These are forecasts to fix or preempt in the PR description, not instructions to please anyone.
113:4. If a pass is clean, say so explicitly. Do not manufacture findings; ~11% of historical review comments were not catchable pre-PR (product/1:1 context) — surface open questions instead of contorting.
114:5. **Record the run** as your last action, only once items 1–4 are complete: `bash ~/.claude/hooks/pre-pr-review-mark.sh <worktree>`. It is the only write this review makes. A hook in the team config blocks `git push` until a run is recorded for the exact code being pushed. The record covers HEAD plus staged and unstaged changes to tracked files, so new files must be staged (`git add -N <file>`) before the review starts. A record means the review ran, not that its findings are resolved: the implementer still fixes or answers them, and any edit after the record needs another run.
---
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Records that /pre-pr-review finished on the code in a worktree, for require-pre-pr-review.sh.
# The record is keyed by the git tree of HEAD plus staged and unstaged changes to tracked files,
# so committing the reviewed changes unchanged keeps it valid and any later edit does not.
set -euo pipefail

cd "${1:-.}"
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

tmp_index="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$tmp_index"' EXIT
cp "$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path index)" "$tmp_index"
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$tmp_index" git add -u
tree="$(GIT_INDEX_FILE="$tmp_index" git write-tree)"

record_dir="$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir)/pre-pr-review"
mkdir -p "$record_dir"
printf 'reviewed %s at HEAD %s on %s\n' "$PWD" "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" >"$record_dir/$tree"
echo "Recorded pre-pr-review for tree $tree"

content.text: Launching the independent Opus review. It only reads code; its one write is the record file that unblocks the push.
